card.title: Environmental impact of the chemical industry

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The chemical industry's footprint splits into gases (SO₂, NOₓ, CO₂, VOCs), liquids (acids, heavy metals, oxygen-demanding organics) and solids (slag, catalysts, plastics) — each with a mobility and a fate that define its harm. Treatment transfers waste between phases (scrubbing turns air into sludge); green chemistry prevents it — atom economy measuring the mass that becomes product, catalysis replacing…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - Atom economy = (mass of desired product ÷ total mass of reactants) × 100% - SO₂ + 2NaOH → Na₂SO₃ + H₂O (alkaline scrubbing) - Yield = (actual ÷ theoretical) × 100% (limiting reactant basis)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Covers only: environmental impact of the chemical industry (within Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Chemistry — don't mix them.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A scrubber converts an air problem into a sludge problem - treatment transfers, prevention eliminates.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***The 100%-yield dirty route*** - a substitution at quantitative yield can still send 70% of its mass out as leaving-group waste: yield and atom economy are independent dials.

rows.text: ## 1. rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Prevention pays twice - less raw material bought and less treatment built; treatment only moves the waste.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Wastes: gas (SO2, NOx, CO2, VOCs), liquid (acids, heavy metals, organics - BOD, eutrophication), solid (slag, catalysts, plastics). Treatments: alkaline scrubbing (SO2 + 2NaOH -> Na2SO3 + H2O), catalytic converters, neutralisation, precipitation, biological treatment, encapsulated landfill.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Regulation sets load AND concentration limits - the same kilo of mercury is a local or a global problem depending on its fate.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 3. Deep Conceptual — Prevention Ranks Above Treatment: Why - Treatment is a *cost* — scrubbers, effluent plants and landfills consume capital and energy while converting one waste into another (a scrubber turns an air problem into a sludge problem).…  ·  ## 4. Deep Conceptual — The Impact Is a Flow, Not a List - Pollutants act through *flows and fates*: SO₂ emitted high travels and returns as acid rain hundreds of kilometres away; mercury discharged to water bioaccumulates up the food chain (Minamata); CO₂ accumulates over decades.…  ·  ### Deep dive — the three media and the response hierarchy Industrial chemistry touches air, water and land. **Air**: SO₂ and NOₓ → acid rain; CO₂ → warming; particulates and VOCs → smog. **Water**: heavy metals (Hg, Cd, Pb), cyanides, and nutrient run-off → eutrophication. **Land**: solid residues, tailings, and persistent organics.…
